name: Columbus
meta_description: TDSC investigative consulting in matters touching Columbus: insurance, banking, logistics and public-contract diligence, Ohio litigation and asset research.
hero_lede: Columbus, Ohio's capital and largest city, combines state government, a major research university, insurance and banking headquarters and a fast-growing logistics and technology base. TDSC supports counsel and companies with research on Columbus counterparties, Franklin County and federal litigation, and Ohio public-sector matters.
intro: Columbus is the capital of Ohio and the state's largest city, with an estimated 933,000 residents in 2024 and about 2.23 million in its metropolitan area. Government is the region's largest employment sector, led by The Ohio State University and the State of Ohio, and JPMorgan Chase is among the largest private employers. Nationwide, Huntington Bancshares and American Electric Power have headquarters downtown, Cardinal Health and Wendy's are based in suburban Dublin, and Abercrombie & Fitch in New Albany. Battelle and OCLC anchor a research economy, and logistics operators use Rickenbacker International Airport alongside John Glenn Columbus International. In 2022 Intel announced plans for semiconductor plants in neighbouring Licking County, backed by about $2 billion in state and local incentives.

Organisations commission investigative work connected to Columbus because of this mix of government, finance and fast growth. State agencies, universities and economic development programmes award contracts and incentives that attract integrity and vendor diligence. Insurers and banks headquartered in the region face claims fraud, employee misconduct and counterparty questions. Distribution and logistics businesses around Rickenbacker raise cargo theft, supplier and contractor issues. Rapid growth in data centres, construction and real estate brings new entrants whose backgrounds need checking. And because Ohio's capital hosts state regulators, the state's highest court and a federal court, Columbus is frequently the forum for litigation that needs background, asset and witness research.

matters.title: Public contract and incentive diligence
matters.text: Researching vendors, contractors and recipients of Ohio state, university or local economic development contracts and incentives: ownership, principals, related companies, prior performance disputes, debarment and political or official connections, for agencies' counterparties, bidders and compliance teams managing procurement and reputational risk.

matters.title: Insurance and financial services matters
matters.text: Supporting Columbus-based insurers, banks and their counsel with claims fraud research, employee and agent misconduct inquiries, and background checks on brokers, agencies and third-party administrators, using public records, court filings and licensing information to establish facts and patterns.

matters.title: Logistics and warehouse counterparty checks
matters.text: Checking freight brokers, carriers, warehouse operators and staffing contractors around Rickenbacker and the region's distribution corridors for ownership, litigation, regulatory history and related-party links, for shippers, insurers and lenders concerned about cargo theft, fraud or contractor reliability.

matters.title: Construction and growth-sector vetting
matters.text: Background research on contractors, developers and suppliers entering the Columbus market on data centre, semiconductor, construction and real estate projects, including mechanics' lien and litigation history, principals' prior business failures and affiliations, before clients commit to subcontracts, joint ventures or financing.

matters.title: Litigation and asset research
matters.text: Supporting counsel in Franklin County and federal proceedings with background on parties and witnesses, corporate histories and asset research covering Ohio entity filings, county property and recorder records, liens and judgments, before trial, settlement or post-judgment enforcement.

local_context.title: Franklin County courts
local_context.text: The Franklin County Court of Common Pleas is the general jurisdiction trial court for Columbus. Franklin County was one of four Ohio counties to pilot a commercial docket from 2008, made permanent under Rules 49 to 49.12 of the Rules of Superintendence, for business-to-business cases such as trade secret, non-compete and shareholder disputes. Appeals go to Ohio's Tenth District Court of Appeals. The county also has municipal and probate courts with their own records.

local_context.title: State capital institutions
local_context.text: As Ohio's capital, Columbus hosts the Supreme Court of Ohio, the Ohio Secretary of State, which registers corporations and limited liability companies, the Ohio Attorney General and state regulators. Secretary of State filings show statutory agents, organisers and status but often not the owners of limited liability companies, so ownership research combines them with court, property and regulatory records.

local_context.title: Federal courts in Columbus
local_context.text: The United States District Court and the United States Bankruptcy Court for the Southern District of Ohio both sit in Columbus, among other cities. They hear securities, fraud, trade secret and other commercial cases and the bankruptcies of central Ohio companies and individuals. Dockets are available through PACER and are a key source for litigation, creditor and insolvency history.

local_context.title: Ohio investigator licensing
local_context.text: Ohio regulates private investigation under Chapter 4749 of the Ohio Revised Code, administered within the Department of Public Safety. Investigation businesses must be licensed, insured and act through a qualifying agent, and their employees registered. Any interviews, surveillance or other field work in Columbus is carried out by investigators licensed in Ohio, coordinated by TDSC with the client's counsel.

local_context.title: County property and lien records
local_context.text: Real property documents in Columbus are recorded by the Franklin County Recorder, and the County Auditor publishes ownership, valuation and tax information by parcel. Many Columbus properties sit in suburbs or adjoining counties such as Delaware and Licking, each with its own recorder and auditor, so property and lien searches are run county by county.

tdsc_approach: TDSC has no office in Columbus and works on Columbus matters from Nashville. Each engagement starts with the purpose agreed with the client or its counsel: vendor or incentive diligence, an insurance or employee matter, a counterparty check, or litigation in Franklin County or the Southern District of Ohio. Research draws on Ohio Secretary of State filings, Franklin and neighbouring county recorder, auditor and court records, PACER, state licensing and regulatory registers and local media, with Fair Credit Reporting Act and other privacy rules applied where relevant. Field work in Ohio is carried out by investigators licensed under Chapter 4749 of the Ohio Revised Code. Reports state sources and confidence so they can support decisions or proceedings.

faqs.q: Which courts handle business disputes in Columbus?
faqs.a: State cases go to the Franklin County Court of Common Pleas, which has a commercial docket for qualifying business-to-business disputes, with appeals to the Tenth District Court of Appeals. Federal cases go to the Southern District of Ohio, which sits in Columbus. Counsel chooses the forum; we tailor research to the court's records and requirements.

faqs.q: Can TDSC vet a company bidding for Ohio public contracts?
faqs.a: Yes. We research the bidder's ownership, principals, related companies, litigation, prior contract performance, debarment or exclusion records and connections to officials, using public and commercial sources. The findings support the client's own procurement or compliance decision. We do not access non-public government systems or personnel records.

faqs.q: How do you find who owns a Columbus LLC?
faqs.a: Ohio Secretary of State filings often name only a statutory agent or organiser. We combine them with county recorder and auditor records, mortgage and lien filings, court cases, licences, permits and media to identify the people behind an LLC, and we state how confident each link is.

faqs.q: Does TDSC carry out surveillance or interviews in Columbus?
faqs.a: TDSC itself works from Nashville. When surveillance, interviews or other field work is justified and lawful, we coordinate investigators licensed in Ohio under Chapter 4749 of the Ohio Revised Code, agree methods with the client's counsel and integrate their findings into our reporting.

faqs.q: What risks come with Columbus's rapid growth?
faqs.a: Large projects in semiconductors, data centres, logistics and housing draw contractors, developers and suppliers new to the region. Common issues include overstated experience, prior business failures under different names, unpaid subcontractor liens and undisclosed related parties. We check these before clients sign subcontracts, leases or financing.
